items.title: آنچه گذشت؛ محسن رضایی: اگر آمریکا حمله کند پایگاه‌های دوردستش را هم هدف قرار می‌دهیم
items.summary: محسن رضایی، دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی ایران، گفته کشورش اجازه خروج «حتی یک ذره» اورانیوم از خاکش را نخواهد داد و همزمان در صورت حمله مجدد نظامی آمریکا به این کشور، ایران اهداف فرامنطقه‌ای را هم در واکنش نظامی خود قرار خواهد داد. همزمان محمدباقر قالیباف تاکید کرده که تنگه هرمز به وضعیت قبل از جنگ باز نخواهد گشت. مسعود پزشکیان هم که برای شرکت در اجلاس اقلیمی به ترکیه رفته است گفته: «هیچ قدرتی حق ندارد به نام امنیت، بنیادهای حیات بر زمین را با خطر مواجه سازد.»

items.title: مجلس خبرگان ایران خواهان بررسی خروج از پیمان منع گسترش سلاح‌های هسته‌ای شد
items.summary: مجلس خبرگان رهبری در ایران گفته است که بررسی خروج از پیمان منع گسترش سلاح‌های هسته‌ای، ان‌پی‌تی، و بازنگری در دکترین دفاعی برای ایجاد بازدارندگی لازم، به «ضرورتی اجتناب‌ناپذیر» و «مطالبه‌ای عمومی و ملی» تبدیل شده است. پیش‌تر، دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا گفت در «جنگ با ایران می‌خواهیم مطمئن شویم که به پیروزی کامل دست می‌یابیم نه پیروزی ۹۳ درصدی.» او در مراسم روز کهنه‌سربازان در گورستان ملی آرلینگتون در ایالت ویرجینیا گفت: «آمریکا جنگ با ایران را آغاز نکرد. ایران از سال ۱۹۷۹ در حال جنگ با آمریکا بوده است.»

items.title: ترامپ تهدید کرد اگر کاروان‌های مهاجران متوقف نشوند، تعرفه‌ها را بر مکزیک دو برابر خواهد کرد

items.summary: دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا از اهرم تعرفه های خود برای ترغیب مکزیک برای جلوگیری از رسیدن کاروان مهاجران به مرز جنوبی ایالات متحده استفاده می کند. ترامپ در یک پست صبح پنجشنبه در شبکه اجتماعی حقیقت نوشت: کاروان های بزرگ در حال تشکیل و راهپیمایی غیرقانونی خود در مکزیک هستند. او افزود: "بسیاری از افراد در این کاروان ها کسانی هستند که کشورهای مختلف نمی خواهند - آنها را به آمریکا بفرستید" - اما آنها پذیرفته نمی شوند! "مکزیک باید آنها را متوقف کند، و اگر این کار را انجام ندهند، تعرفه های مکزیک فوراً دو برابر خواهد شد." فرماندار تگزاس، گشت مرزی بزرگ ما، یخ، بسیار مطلع شده است. هیچ مسامحه ای وجود نخواهد داشت!» پست ترامپ با این پیشنهاد آغاز شد که نتایج انتخابات میان دوره ای تلاش های مهاجرت گسترده را جسورتر کرده است.
items.summary_original: President Donald Trump is using his tariff leverage to urge Mexico to stop a migrant caravan from reaching the U.S. southern border. "Huge CARAVANS are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico," Trump wrote in a Thursday morning Truth Social post. "Many of the people in these Caravans are those that various countries don’t want - ‘Send them to America,’ they say - But they will not be accepted! "MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED," he added. "MEXICO, THE GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, THE VERY LIBERAL NEW GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, OUR GREAT BORDER PATROL, ICE, HAVE BEEN SO INFORMED. There will be no leniency!" Trump's post began with the suggestion the midterm election results have emboldened the mass migration efforts that he has had to shut down since his first administration. "Here we go again!" Trump's post began. "With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms - I WAS NOT ON THE BALLOT- the INVASION of our Country is taking place again." The group of migrants, an estimated 1,500 people mostly from Central America, set off Tuesday from the southern city of Tapachula near the Guatemala border, hoping Democrats' victory in the U.S. midterm election could open pathways for them to live and work in the United States. Reuters contributed to this report.

items.summary_original: Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola lost in her legal effort to get access to records identifying rejected absentee ballots during the ongoing count, and then lost some of her narrow lead in the latest ballot drop Wednesday night. An Alaska judge on Wednesday ruled against the Peltola campaign’s request for the records in the midterm's final uncalled Senate race, ruling the demand was "simply not reasonable" while election officials continue counting votes. Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews sided with the Alaska Division of Elections, finding the agency is "currently busy processing ballots from the 2026 general election" and "simply lacks the capacity to generate the report" from the voter registration database. "Even if the request were otherwise considered reasonable outside the peak election time of year, it is simply not reasonable nor required right now," Matthews wrote, adding that "the timing of the Campaign’s request could simply not be worse." MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT Peltola’s campaign had sued last week seeking information about which absentee ballots were flagged for rejection and why. Campaign attorney Abha Kelly told the court the process was "going incredibly smoothly" and that the campaign was not seeking confidential data or trying to disrupt the count. She argued the request would simply centralize transparency that observers already have in a decentralized way. DUNL

items.summary_original: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Tuesday he supports bringing deported DACA recipients back to the U.S. and providing what he called "remedial assistance," prompting critics to accuse him of wanting to pay deported immigrants. Jeffries replied "certainly" when asked during a "PBS NewsHour" interview whether he would support bringing deported DACA recipients back to the U.S. He also said those he believes were treated unfairly by the Trump administration should receive "remedial assistance." "Anyone, whether they are a citizen, whether they were here lawfully, whether they're DACA recipients, who've been treated unfairly and unjustly by the administration, we need to provide remedial assistance to them and undo the damage that's been done to the country, to law-abiding immigrant families and to the American people over this last 20 months or so," Jeffries told PBS News. JEFFRIES VOWS DEMOCRATS WON’T ‘GIVE A DIME’ TO TRUMP’S DEPORTATION EFFORTS DACA offers eligible immigrants brought to the country illegally as children temporary protection from deportation and the ability to apply for work authorization, but does not grant legal immigration status, according to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Jeffries did not specify whether the "remedial assistance" he proposed would include financial compensation. items.summary_original: The aftershocks of last week's midterm elections are still being felt by Senate Republicans, but another political reality is beginning to set in: The GOP may not regain control of the chamber for years to come. This year’s Senate map was, initially, favorable to Republicans in their quest to maintain and possibly grow their 53-seat majority in the Senate. But the next election cycle’s map in 2028 is tough, perhaps even insurmountable, for Republicans to conquer. The Senate GOP’s newly minted campaign chief, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, acknowledged that the map to reclaim the majority in 2028 is "very tough." Democrats only have three incumbents up for re-election in battleground states, while Republicans have to defend seats in a slew of once-safe, deep-red states, including both Carolinas, Kansas and Iowa, among several others. His home state, which just turned a shade of purple with Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown’s victory over Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, is in play again, too. Moreno, when asked to sketch a 30,000-foot view of what the future fight for power would look like, told Fox News Digital that Republicans had "dealt with tough situations before." "Look, it is an absolutely brutal map, but, politics, things change pretty quickly," Moreno said. "So we'll see how it is, but we're gonna be extraordinarily disciplined, we're gonna be extremely honest with our data. "We've got to have accountability, and then we also have to increase the minimum wage," Khanna said. items.summary_original: A Florida city says it cannot host its annual St. Patrick's Day Parade or Pride event in 2027 because of a new Republican-backed state law restricting local governments from funding, promoting or taking official action related to diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives. Officials in Delray Beach announced the decision Tuesday, citing restrictions on "certain programming and activities designed or implemented with reference to ethnicity, sexual orientation or gender identity." "Following a review of the legislation and its requirements, the City has determined that it is legally prohibited from organizing, funding, or promoting these events in 2027," the city said in a statement. "The City recognizes that these annual events have provided opportunities for members of the community to gather, celebrate, and connect. We appreciate the residents, participants, volunteers, and community partners who have contributed to these events over the years," the statement added. items.summary_original: Sen. Jim Justice, R-W. Va., said the GOP can "forget" about taking back the Senate majority in 2028 after Democrats' blue wave secured the majority in both chambers of Congress following last week's midterm elections. Eight Republican-held Senate seats were flipped, bringing the Democratic caucus to 55 seats after Democrat Scott Colom was projected on Wednesday to win Mississippi’s Senate race. The caucus could gain another seat if Democrat Mary Peltola holds onto her narrow lead in Alaska. "You can forget 2028. Absolutely," Justice told the Washington Examiner of the next federal election . "I hope and pray we don’t lose the presidency. But this is such a colossal blow that it is beyond belief how colossal this is to America," he continued. GOP EYES SENATE COMEBACK AFTER DEMOCRATIC BLOODBATH, BUT ANOTHER POLITICAL NIGHTMARE COULD AWAIT Justice joined President Donald Trump , Vice President JD Vance, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other Republicans in partially attributing the party's midterm losses to the war in Iran, which led to surging fuel prices. Gas prices are nearly 90 cents per gallon higher than a year ago, according to AAA, which listed the national average at about $3.94 per gallon on Wednesday, compared with $3.07 a year earlier. "Obviously, the election result was not what we hoped for," Thune told reporters earlier this week. Rony Alexander Gomez-Alberto, 34, was granted asylum by an immigration judge after his third attempted illegal entry into the United States in 2019, according to DHS, which accused him of exploiting weaknesses in the asylum system. In an excerpt of his asylum application provided by DHS, Gomez-Alberto checked "Yes" when asked whether he feared harm or mistreatment if returned to his home country. TRUMP PUTS ASYLUM LAWYERS ‘ON NOTICE’ WITH NEW FRONT IN WAR ON FRAUD "I am also afraid that I will be killed — either by private citizens or the police — in both of these countries because I am transgender," he allegedly wrote, according to the application. "This criminal illegal alien attempted to storm the cockpit, hijack a plane and claimed he had a bomb. Thanks to law enforcement, he is now behind bars," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement. "This twice-deported criminal illegal alien was allowed into our country because of a weak asylum system that allowed him to game the system." items.summary_original: El Salvador's president on Tuesday said the country's military helped deliver a devastating air assault against the headquarters of one of Haiti's most powerful criminal gangs, which has been linked to mass kidnappings, weapons trafficking and extortion. Airstrikes targeted strongholds belonging to 400 Mawozo and the home of its leader, Lanmò San Jou, Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said. The attack took place Sunday near Port-au-Prince and was carried out by a Haitian police task force backed by Salvadoran troops, The Miami Herald reported . BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR The operation appears to be part of an ongoing military effort in response to the disappearance of four Salvadoran members of a U .N.-backed security mission abducted in a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince Oct. 18. "We kept our promise," Bukele said in a post on X. Videos showed several helicopters launching airstrikes against multiple compounds inside sprawling complexes. Dozens of people were also seen fleeing the properties on foot and motorbikes after the strikes. "Most of them ran away without even trying to fight. What cowards!" Bukele said. As many as 20 people are believed to have been killed in the operation, according to The Miami Herald, citing anonymous sources. items.summary_original: Familiar faces populate the 110-plus new members of Congress . A few "freshmen" are returning to the House. Even if they’ve been gone for a while. There’s Rep.-elect Hilda Solis, D-Calif., who last served in Congress in 2009. She departed to become President Obama’s labor secretary. Rep.-elect Jerry Carl, R-Ala., just left Capitol Hill early last year after losing a primary to Rep. Barry Moore, R-Ala., who is now moving to the Senate. REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: A DEMOCRATIC MAJORITY COULD EXPOSE THE LIMITS OF THE PROGRESSIVE AGENDA And then there’s Rep.-elect Melissa Bean, D-Ill. She first won a seat in the House in 2004 and lost in 2010. Now, Bean is back. Her advice to the rookies? "Make sure you get a really good scheduler and that they schedule eating because your staff will run you all day long," Bean said. "You're kind of like the football that they pass from one staff member to the other. The whole day goes by, and you’re starving." House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., is on track to become House speaker in January. But some progressives are holding out. Bean was a moderate when she served before. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., is projected to lose her bid for a second full term in the U.S. Senate to state District Attorney Scott Colom in a race that was deadlocked until the final weeks of October, according to The Associated Press. More than a week after Election Day, the AP called the razor-thin race in favor of Colom Wednesday, pushing the Democrats' hold on the U.S. Senate to 55 seats to the Republicans' 44 in another flip. SOROS NETWORK TARGETS DEEP-RED MISSISSIPPI IN BID TO FLIP SENATE SEAT Democrats could gain another pending the results in Alaska, where former Rep. Mary Peltola is in a neck-and-neck contest with Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska. A source told Fox News Digital Hyde-Smith had spoken with Colom and conceded the race. Colom's victory over Hyde-Smith marked a historic moment in the Magnolia State, which hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since the 1980s. Hyde-Smith, in a video posted to X, said, "While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters. "I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state." items.summary_original: Iran claims it struck a small Omani island in the Strait of Hormuz , targeting oil tanker navigation infrastructure as CENTCOM maintains its blockade of Iranian ports and protects commercial shipping from Iranian attacks along the southern route. Three sources also confirmed to Reuters Wednesday that navigation systems and communications equipment on Didamar Island, also known as Little Quoin Island, had been attacked, raising concerns about the vulnerability of maritime infrastructure used to maintain oil shipments through the Gulf. Iran's semiofficial Fars News Agency reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy targeted the island, alleging the systems were being used to help vessels transit the strait without Tehran's authorization. WHITE HOUSE SILENT ON IRAN-OMAN HORMUZ PLAN TEHRAN SAYS WOULD BAN US WARSHIPS Iranian state television also claimed that personnel and equipment on the island "were helping the flow of oil smuggling by the enemy," with the IRGC maintaining it had carried out the strikes, Reuters reported. Video published by Reuters showed smoke rising near the rocky outcrop. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) said it identified the attack as occurring Nov. 8, before Iranian state media claimed responsibility on Nov. 10. ISW also questioned the extent of the reported damage, noting that commercial vessels continued using the southern route after the attack. items.summary_original: Unruly protesters set fires, smashed storefronts and launched fireworks at riot police across parts of Spain on Wednesday as a massive nationwide strike over soaring housing costs disrupted transportation and businesses. Violent scenes unfolded in Barcelona, where some demonstrators vandalized stores along the city's popular Paseo de Gracia shopping boulevard, set small bonfires and launched fireworks at officers arriving in riot gear and armored vehicles, according to The Associated Press . The violence erupted after a largely peaceful march as Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years, with workers demanding relief from skyrocketing rents and the rising cost of living. TRAVELERS MAY FACE MAJOR DISRUPTIONS AS STRIKES THREATEN AIRPORTS AND POPULAR ATTRACTIONS Housing activists claimed 400,000 people marched through Barcelona, while city officials estimated attendance at 55,000. Government officials reported another 120,000 demonstrators gathered in Madrid despite heavy rain, the AP reported. The nationwide walkout disrupted public transportation, forced some businesses to close and blocked major roads. Police made arrests across the country, while officers used pepper spray against demonstrators in Madrid, according to the AP. items.summary_original: House Majority Leader Steve Scalise , R-La., the No. 2 Republican in the House of Representatives and the most tenured figure among the chamber's party leadership, declined to say whether he would commit to serving the full term in the upcoming 120th Congress. "There’s no decision on what’s next," Scalise said on Wednesday. "I’ve got to get through these next few weeks, and then we have a lot of decisions to make about what's life going to look like in the minority. But I sure still have a great passion for this country." JIM JORDAN THROWS HAT IN RING FOR HOUSE MINORITY LEADER AS GOP PICKS UP PIECES AFTER BLUE WAVE Scalise’s answer follows a loss to Rep. Jim Jordan , R-Ohio, in a bid to become the party’s new minority leader. His defeat now forces Scalise to decide whether he intends to retire or remain on Capitol Hill as a rank-and-file member of the minority as Democrats retake control of the House in January. For now, Scalise stressed that he remains focused on securing GOP priorities before the new year. "There’s a lot more for us to do. We have a few weeks left in the lame duck [session] and, frankly, a few big, big issues ahead. I want to see us do as much as we possibly can while we still have this majority," Scalise said. "I’ve got a lot more gas in the tank. Obviously, all of us know there’s some real change coming in January. We still have work to do right now." items.summary: مقامات روز سه‌شنبه اعلام کردند که چهار خرس گریزلی از طریق شواهد DNA با حمله مرگبار به یک مادر و دختر در بریتیش کلمبیا مرتبط هستند که باعث شد افسران حیات‌وحش کانادایی هر چهار حیوان را بکشند. سرویس افسر حفاظت از بریتیش کلمبیا گفت که آزمایشات پزشکی قانونی به طور قطعی یک گریزلی ماده بالغ و سه فرزندش را با مرگ جنیفر بالکاراس، 48 ساله، و دخترش، سله رید، 20 ساله، در نزدیکی بلا کولا مرتبط دانست. بر اساس بیانیه 10 نوامبر آژانس، خرس ها در آخر هفته دستگیر و بر اساس دستورالعمل های استانی واکنش درگیری انسان و حیات وحش برای حفاظت از امنیت عمومی کشته شدند. جسد کوهنورد گمشده در خارج از مسیر کشف شد زیرا بازرسان به بررسی برخورد نادر مرگبار خرس می پردازند محققان تشخیص دادند که این برخورد احتمالاً شامل
items.summary_original: Four grizzly bears have been linked through DNA evidence to a deadly attack on a mother and daughter in British Columbia , prompting Canadian wildlife officers to kill all four animals, officials announced Tuesday. The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said forensic testing conclusively linked an adult female grizzly and her three offspring to the deaths of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, near Bella Coola. The bears were captured over the weekend and killed in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety, according to a Nov. 10 statement from the agency. BODY OF MISSING HIKER DISCOVERED OFF TRAIL AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE RARE DEADLY BEAR ENCOUNTER Investigators determined that the encounter likely involved predatory behavior, although officials did not elaborate on how the attack unfolded. "This was a heartbreaking event for the families, the Nuxalk Nation and the Bella Coola community. We hope the efforts of everyone who responded, along with these findings, bring some measure of closure," said Insp. Jeff Tyre in a news briefing. More than a dozen conservation officers participated in the response, helping recover the victims, collect evidence and locate the bears while working in difficult terrain and weather conditions. "A distinguished diplomat, experienced leader, kind colleague, and mentor has departed this life. A consummate professional and brilliant Americanist, A.N. Darchiev served on one of the most critical and demanding fronts of Russian foreign policy." "We express our deepest and most sincere condolences to the family and loved ones of Alexander Nikitich Darchiev," the statement added. "The cherished memory of our untimely departed colleague will forever remain in our hearts." We won. Now the question is when we want to end. We must have a total victory. Not a 93% victory. It's going to be total," he continued. Trump noted that of the roughly seven months of conflict, "only a few weeks were active fighting," but he acknowledged the casualties America sustained. "We lost 18 beautiful souls," Trump said. items.summary_original: The share of military veterans in Congress is projected to fall to its lowest level in decades in the incoming 120th Congress, but while overall veteran representation continues a long-term decline, the partisan composition of the freshman class marks a sharp contrast. Democrats are bringing roughly three times as many first-time veteran members as Republicans, and they are catching up among House members overall. Still, as America marks Veterans Day, the numbers show the institutional voice of military service in the legislative branch is heading toward its lowest watermark in modern history. AFTER GOP'S BRUTAL MIDTERMS, ‘CHUCK NORRIS OF FLORIDA POLITICS’ TELLS PARTY TO 'GET UP AND FIGHT' Analysis from With Honor Action and Military Times indicates veterans will hold roughly 15% of seats when the new Congress convenes in January, down from about 19% in the outgoing body and well below the 27% recorded in 2001 before the war on terror began. That comes despite a record number of veterans running in 2026, according to the analysis. In January 2025, there were just 28 Democrats compared to 72 Republicans, according to Military Times . Among the 79 projected for the 120th Congress, the partisan gap is closing to 33 Democrats and 46 Republicans. items.summary_original: Israel's newly elected parliament was sworn in Tuesday, marking the beginning of a political transition that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure in power. Despite the opposition's parliamentary gains, the country remains without a new government, and negotiations to form one face significant obstacles. At the center of those negotiations is former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog on Sunday with assembling Israel's next governing coalition after 67 lawmakers recommended him for the position, compared with 46 who supported Netanyahu. Although Eisenkot's Yashar party won 21 seats in the Oct. 27 election , he is working closely with former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, whose B'Yachad party, formed with former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, secured another 12 seats. NETANYAHU FACES COALITION SHOWDOWN AS RIVALS MANEUVER TO FORM ISRAEL'S NEXT GOVERNMENT The two parties have not merged, but their cooperation effectively gives Eisenkot the negotiating backing of 33 lawmakers — more than Netanyahu's Likud, which remains the largest individual party in the Knesset with 27 seats. A source with knowledge of discussions within the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu told Fox News Digital that Bennett has decided to act as a political kingmaker, supporting Eisenkot's leadership bid rather than seeking the premiership himself. Massie, R-Ky., told Fox News Digital that while he could not substantiate allegations that Hegseth improperly withheld military assistance to Ukraine, he believes Democrats will investigate the matter and potentially introduce additional articles of impeachment when they take control of Congress in January. "I believe [Democrats] may use some of the same articles of impeachment when they're in the majority, but I also believe there are gonna be some other articles of impeachment based on hearings and committees," Massie told Fox News Digital. "I think the Democrats will do that." Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., told Fox News Digital on Tuesday she was never informed by federal agencies of the grounds on which she is being investigated — even claiming she isn’t sure how many probes into her there are. "No, no," she said when asked if she had been told exactly the basis for the investigations. There are two known ongoing federal probes into the Somali-born congresswoman — the first, confirmed by sources to Fox News Digital, is the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) looking into whether her immigration paperwork was fraudulently filled out by herself or her father; and the second is investigating her financial disclosures discrepancies and was confirmed publicly by U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro. "I’m not sure," Omar said. "You probably have more details on that." items.summary_original: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — In a historic house near Dubai Creek, a small gallery commemorating the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust stands alongside collections exploring Islamic civilization, Emirati heritage and the history of Palestine and the Holy Land. The Holocaust exhibition at the privately owned Crossroads of Civilizations Museum is among the first permanent displays of its kind in the Arab world. Opened in May 2021, less than a year after the UAE normalized relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords, it has become a symbol of the Emirates' approach to religious coexistence. During a recent visit to the museum, Fox News Digital saw displays documenting Nazi persecution, including a life-size image of the boy from the famous Warsaw Ghetto photograph, his hands raised in surrender. The gallery also tells the stories of Muslims who rescued Jews during the Holocaust, including Egyptian physician Mohammed Helmy, who sheltered Jews from Nazi persecution in Berlin. US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS But the story behind the exhibition is as personal as the objects it preserves. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, museum founder Ahmed Obaid Al Mansoori, a former member of the UAE's Federal National Council, explained that his passion for collecting historical artifacts began in childhood, when he inherited family manuscripts and objects from his grandparents. items.summary_original: The U.S. Air Force abruptly relocated more than a dozen aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England amid an emerging security threat, U.S. officials confirmed Tuesday. The Wall Street Journal first reported the move, citing sources who said the threat originated in Iran. As U.S. officials assessed the threat's nature and urgency, commanders raised the base's security level to Force Protection Condition Charlie, the military's second-highest alert level, indicating a likely terrorist threat against personnel or facilities. IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS Flight-tracking data and open-source analysts with the Military Air Tracking Alliance identified 13 U.S. aircraft leaving the base late Monday, the Associated Press said. Nine Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers were moved to airfields in Scotland, Germany and Spain. Three CV-22B Ospreys were relocated to nearby RAF Lakenheath, which has hardened aircraft shelters. A U.S. official told The Associated Press the moves were precautionary, noting that some aircraft were on rotational deployments while others were permanently stationed in the United Kingdom . IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY The move marks the second major relocation of U.S. military aircraft from Britain in less than two months. items.summary_original: A 7-year-old girl with dual U.S. and Mexican citizenship was shot and killed during a Mexican security operation targeting an alleged cartel member, and her mother accused police officers aboard a helicopter of firing the deadly shot. Aranza Aidelany Pardo died Oct. 29 in Matamoros, a Mexican border city across from Brownsville, Texas. She was among six people killed during the operation and subsequent roadblocks erected by the Gulf Cartel, according to The Associated Press. Her mother, Claudia Pardo García, told the AP that gunfire from a Tamaulipas state police helicopter struck her daughter in the head. Pardo was also wounded in the leg. Mexican authorities are investigating three officers aboard the helicopter who remain on active duty, according to Tamaulipas Public Security Secretary Carlos Arturo Pancardo. EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS The operation resulted in the arrest of Axel Alfredo Cárdenas Rodríguez, also known as El Titán, the son of an alleged Gulf Cartel leader and nephew of the group's imprisoned founder, Osiel Cárdenas Guillén. Pardo told the AP that she, her husband and their five children were returning home when they encountered cartel roadblocks and took a rural shortcut. She said a police helicopter began following their vehicle before circling in front of it. Her husband exited with his hands raised to show officers they were a family, but gunfire erupted. items.title_original: Senior US Army soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
items.summary: به گفته پلیس بریتانیا، یک سرباز ارشد ارتش آمریکا روز سه شنبه در انگلیس به ظن جرایم جاسوسی مرتبط با روسیه دستگیر شد. به گفته پلیس متروپولیتن، مرد 41 ساله که هویتش فاش نشده است، در چارچوب تحقیقات در مورد تهدیدات مظنون به امنیت ملی که توسط پلیس مبارزه با تروریسم هدایت می شد، بازداشت شد. مقامات گفتند که این دستگیری با هماهنگی ارتش ایالات متحده و FBI انجام شده است. کش پاتل، مدیر اف‌بی‌آی در بیانیه‌ای گفت: این دستگیری مهم شامل اتهامات جاسوسی است که برای ایالات متحده و متحدان ما بسیار نگران کننده است. FBI برای مامور سابق اطلاعات نیروی هوایی متهم به جاسوسی برای ایران 200 هزار دلار جایزه می دهد.
items.summary_original: A senior U.S. Army soldier was arrested in England Tuesday on suspicion of espionage offenses related to Russia, according to U.K. police. The 41-year-old man, whose identity was not released, was detained as part of an investigation into suspected national security threats led by Counter Terrorism Policing , according to the Metropolitan Police. Officials said the arrest was carried out in coordination with the U.S. military and the FBI. "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. Mohsen Rezaei, a former commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), now serves as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and acts as a key aide to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. He also helped shape Tehran's military strategy during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq War . That eight-year conflict ended after Iran's then-supreme leader, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, accepted a U.N.-brokered cease-fire that he famously likened to drinking from a "poisoned chalice." JD VANCE RETURNS TO WASHINGTON AFTER 16 HOURS OF IRAN PEACE TALKS COLLAPSE IN PAKISTAN "Ceasefire means an unfinished war," Rezaei had said of the war in a 2006 interview with the Iranian publication Baztab. An English translation of the interview is preserved by George Washington University's National Security Archive . Asked whether both sides would remain in their positions and begin talks, Rezaei replied: "Yes. Negotiations can take 30 to 40 years and during that time Iran and Iraq should be prepared to fight." items.summary_original: The husband of a TV anchor was arrested in Pakistan Sunday after his wife was found dead with a gunshot wound to the head, according to officials. Rabiya Ahsan, 41, was allegedly killed inside her home in Rawalpindi, according to Punjab Information Minister Azma Zahid Bokhari. Ahsan worked as a program host for 92 News, where she established herself as a dedicated journalist alongside senior colleagues. She also frequently posted videos about national affairs on social media. Officials identified her husband as Ahsan Tahir Khan, who claimed he was playing with a firearm in the home when it accidentally discharged, Bokhari said. Police are preparing to pursue a murder case against the suspect , according to the report. Rawalpindi police also confirmed in a post on X that a woman was killed in a Sunday shooting but did not immediately identify her. Authorities said officers seized the suspected weapon in connection with the husband's arrest. Ahsan's body was also transferred to a hospital for a postmortem examination. items.summary: سرعت راه رفتن می‌تواند سرنخ‌هایی مهم درباره سلامت جسمی و شناختی افراد در اختیار ما بگذارد. پژوهش‌ها نشان داده‌اند که کندتر راه رفتن فقط نشانه افزایش سن نیست، بلکه ممکن است با خطر بیشتر بیماری، افت عملکرد مغز و حتی کاهش امید به زندگی ارتباط داشته باشد. به گفته پژوهشگران، سرعت گام برداشتن بازتابی از عملکرد مجموعه‌ای از دستگاه‌های بدن، از مغز و اعصاب گرفته تا قلب، ریه‌ها، عضلات و استخوان‌هاست. به همین دلیل، برخی دانشمندان آن را یکی از ساده‌ترین و در عین حال موثرترین شاخص‌ها برای ارزیابی سلامت و روند پیری بدن می‌دانند.

items.summary_original: ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — President Donald Trump met Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, on Monday at the White House as diplomatic efforts to end the war with Iran continue, even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio warns that negotiations remain far from a breakthrough and Tehran signals a willingness to negotiate without yielding to pressure. The competing messages come as the Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of global economic disruption and regional governments push for a diplomatic solution to a conflict that has subjected Gulf countries to thousands of Iranian missile and drone attacks . Speaking to reporters Sunday before departing for a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Rubio said there had been little progress in negotiations and rejected the terms put forward by Tehran. "I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said. RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY' He emphasized that Trump prefers a diplomatic settlement but described Iran's demands as unrealistic. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that Tehran was prepared to negotiate an end to what he described as a prolonged state of neither war nor peace. items.summary: به گفته مقامات، مرد مسلحی که در تیراندازی در یک میدان شلوغ در لهستان شش نفر را کشت و 15 نفر را زخمی کرد، روز دوشنبه پس از شلیک پلیس در جریان این حمله جان باخت. مظنون 24 ساله از تیراندازی روز شنبه در کراکوف در شرایط وخیم در بیمارستان بستری بود و قبل از مرگ تحت چندین عمل جراحی قرار گرفت. دادستان لهستان تحقیقاتی را در مورد قتل و اقدام به قتل، از جمله حمله به افسران پلیس، به عنوان یک جرم تروریستی احتمالی آغاز کرده است. مقامات گفتند که فرد مسلح دارای دیدگاه های راست افراطی بود، اگرچه بازرسان به طور علنی انگیزه این حمله را مشخص نکرده اند. نوجوانی که کلاه ایمنی بر سر داشت، کارگر مدرسه لهستان را در میان ترس از حملات کپی‌برداری کشت، پلیس همچنین اجساد مادر، پدر و خواهر مظنون را در خانه خانواده کشف کرد.
items.summary_original: The gunman who killed six people and wounded 15 others in a shooting at a crowded square in Poland died Monday after being shot by police during the attack, authorities said. The 24-year-old suspect had been hospitalized in critical condition since Saturday's shooting in Krakow and underwent several operations before his death. Polish prosecutors have opened an investigation into the killings and attempted killings, including attacks on police officers, as a possible terrorist offense. Authorities said the gunman held far-right views , though investigators have not publicly established a motive for the attack. TEEN WEARING HELMET CAMERA KILLS WORKER AT POLISH SCHOOL AMID FEARS OF COPYCAT ATTACKS Police also discovered the bodies of the suspect's mother, father and sister at the family's home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, roughly 93 miles northeast of Krakow, per reporting from The Associated Press. The three are believed to have died from gunshot wounds, though authorities have not confirmed the circumstances of their deaths. The suspect, who was wearing military-style clothing and a bulletproof vest, drove into Krakow's historic Main Square on Saturday before opening fire, according to authorities. Four women and two men were killed, including a British man and an Austrian woman. Five foreign nationals were among the wounded. Herzog announced his decision on Nov. 7, but the formal presentation of the mandate is scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 8, at 5 p.m. Israeli time. Eisenkot will then have 28 days to assemble a government, with a possible 14-day extension. The decision could mark a significant step toward ending Netanyahu’s tenure, but it would also launch a difficult round of coalition negotiations, with deep disagreements among parties seeking to replace him. Netanyahu received the backing of 46 lawmakers, while seven members of the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party declined to endorse either candidate. "The results of the consultations may appear clear," Herzog said in his Nov. 5 statement, but cautioned that competing political demands and vetoes have left the prospects for forming a government uncertain. "That these elements characterize a particular and serious risk to public institutions, agent safety, and the normal functioning of public services during such demonstrations," the statement continued. items.summary_original: Małopolska Police and MPK S.A. confirmed a Polish gunman opened fire at a popular tourist destination in Kraków Saturday, killing six people and wounding at least 15 more. Of the six dead, four are women and two are men, according to Małopolska Police. Shooting from a moving vehicle, the gunman allegedly targeted people at random, injuring civilians as well as police during the attack on Kraków's bustling Main Square. TEEN WEARING HELMET CAMERA KILLS WORKER AT POLISH SCHOOL AMID FEARS OF COPYCAT ATTACKS "Six people were killed and fifteen were injured in the incident in the Main Market Square, the Małopolska Provincial Office reported. The perpetrator of the attack was shot and detained by police officers. Rescue services are still working at the scene," MPK S.A., the city's municipal public transport company, wrote in a statement shared to X. Video posted on social media showed people running while gunshots rang out. Police shot and wounded the suspect during a gunfight, and the area is now secured, according to authorities. The suspect, who has only been identified by police as a "citizen of the Republic of Poland," was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-style rifle to carry out the attack, Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Kraków police, told Polish network TVN24. items.summary_original: First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire. "We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark." "Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity." INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians. Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev , who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting. items.summary_original: France deployed 70,000 police officers Thursday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets for nationwide strikes and protests after left-wing groups called for a mobilization. In Paris, the Eiffel Tower was closed; in Lyon, French riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters; and near Toulouse, a high school was set on fire, according to Reuters. "We need to turn up in big numbers on the streets today," the news agency quoted the head of the left-wing CGT union Sophie Binet as saying. The demonstrations come after France was rocked by violent protests in October, which outgoing French President Emmanuel Macron blamed on "ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic." FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC' An official close to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that by early Thursday, around 270,000 people had joined the union action in 180 rallies outside the capital. About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate, some because of student blockades and others because teachers were on strike, The Associated Press reported. Toby Harris, an Australian tourist who was visiting Paris on Thursday, told Fox News Digital that "I feel like it's probably a good thing that there's like political action in the city. items.summary: چندین هواپیما در سرتاسر اروپا روز پنجشنبه به دلیل تهدیدهای بمب گذاری که بی اساس بودند منحرف شدند و مجبور به فرود اضطراری شدند. حداقل 11 هواپیما از شهرهایی از جمله کپنهاگ، دوبلین، هلسینکی، مادرید، میلان و ورشو آسیب دیده اند. منبع تهدیدات بلافاصله مشخص نشد. این حوادث پس از آن رخ داد که چندین پرواز در اروپا در روز سه‌شنبه هشدارهای مشابهی دریافت کردند که دولت بریتانیا آن را "تهدیدهای جعلی بدخواهانه" توصیف کرد. پلیس چک پیش از این که بازرسی های هواپیما را بازرسی کرد، نوشت: "با دریافت تهدیدی مبنی بر قرار دادن یک بمب دست ساز در 4 هواپیمای عازم پراگ، به همراه همکاران فرودگاه پراگ برای فرود آنها آماده می شویم. ما ارتباط تهدیدات را کم ارزیابی می کنیم."
items.summary_original: Multiple planes across Europe were diverted and forced to make emergency landings Thursday because of bomb threats that have turned out to be unfounded. At least 11 planes, originating from cities including Copenhagen, Dublin, Helsinki, Madrid, Milan and Warsaw, have been affected. The source of the threats was not immediately clear. These incidents came after several flights in Europe received similar warnings on Tuesday that the U.K. government described as "malicious hoax threats." "Upon receiving a threat regarding the placement of an improvised explosive device on board 4 aircraft heading to Prague, we are preparing with colleagues from Prague Airport for their landing. We assess the relevance of the threats as low," Czech Police wrote on X, before adding that inspections of the planes yielded "negative results." The threats come at a time when European officials have been blaming Russia and Iran for "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage, which both Moscow and Tehran deny, Reuters reported. RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT Earlier, a flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to a military air base in western France because of a bomb threat, according to French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office. That flight landed safely at the base in Evreux in Normandy, with all 151 passengers and six crew members disembarking, the office said.
